title: Tenant Snapline: compact status strip with topology flares for Private Console
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Design brief:
We need a lightweight, single-line status surface ("Snapline") for the Private Console tenant/cluster listing that communicates critical health and network signals at a glance and expands into small topology 'flares' for immediate context and quick actions. The goal is to reduce triage time for platform operators by surfacing high-priority state (eg. degraded network paths, pending upgrades, egress spikes, eviction risk) without requiring a full drill-in to the cluster detail page.

Scope:
- A compact horizontal strip shown in tenant and cluster lists with up to 5 micro-indicators (health, latency, egress, upgrade-state, maintenance-window).
- Click/hover expands a contextual flare anchored to the strip showing a mini-topology (peer region, primary route, recent packet loss) and 1–2 quick actions (acknowledge, open maintenance window editor, trigger emergency rollback).
- Integrates with rollouts UI: when a canary/upgrade is in-progress, the Snapline shows rollout progress and a one-click pause/rollback affordance.
- Designed for the Private/VPC console where space is constrained and customers require compact, actionable overviews.

Design goals & success metrics:
- Visually compact: take <= 40px height in list rows at default density.
- Reduce mean time to first action (MTFA) for critical incidents in Private clusters by 30% in pilot.
- No more than 2 clicks from sighting an anomaly to performing the primary remediation action.
- Accessible: contrast, keyboard focus, screen-reader announcements on expansion/collapses.

Deliverables/prototypes:
- Figma prototype: Snapline default state, hover expansion mock, flare mini-topology, and quick-action flows. Link in attachments.
- Annotated interaction spec for engineers: animation timings (150ms expand), data refresh cadence (5s for high-criticality signals), and fallback behavior when telemetry is missing.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Density vs clarity: we favor a single-line micro-indicator over cramming full textual status to avoid layout breakage in long tenant lists. Full textual descriptions remain in the details panel.
- Real-time refresh: aggressive polling (5s) for critical signals improves awareness but increases backend load. Proposal: use a push/subscribe channel for high-priority tenants and 30s polling otherwise. This requires backend work (see dependencies).
- Quick actions: exposing rollback/pause directly reduces reaction time but elevates risk of accidental triggers. Mitigation: require a short confirmation toast and use progressive disclosure (show full rollback only on a long-press option or secondary modal).

Accessibility notes:
- All micro-indicators must have aria-labels and a single aggregate status label for screen readers.
- Keyboard order: focusable Snapline -> open flare -> actions within flare -> close.

Integration & backend dependencies:
- ENG-239812: telemetry streaming for per-tenant packet loss and egress spike signals.
- ENG-240101: rollout action API to pause/rollback canary deployments.
- PM-447: product decision on which quick actions to expose in a default tenant config.

Rollout plan:
1) Ship as opt-in beta for 5 enterprise tenants (feature flag).
2) Collect MTFA and false-positive rates for 4 weeks.
3) Iterate visual weighting and thresholds based on ops feedback.
4) Promote to on-by-default in console-2026.05 if metrics meet targets.

Open questions for review:
- Should the Snapline be configurable per-tenant (which micro-indicators are shown)? PM leans yes for enterprise customers.
- Confirm allowable quick actions for customers under stricter RBAC (Private deployments with limited edit permissions).

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma prototype reviewed and signed off by PM and an engineering owner.
- Engineering acceptance doc created listing required telemetry endpoints with expected shapes and SLAs.
- Accessibility checklist completed with keyboard and screen-reader testing.

References and artifacts are in attachments.
